scope.flow: TrailsRouter public execute/pullAmountAndExecute using delegatecall to Multicall3 aggregate3Value to move router-held funds
scope.environment: EVM smart contract (TrailsRouter with delegated Multicall3)

statements.text: TrailsRouter delegatecalls Multicall3 aggregate3Value, permitting arbitrary targets and ETH values drawn from address(this).
The router can hold nonzero residual ETH and/or ERC20 funds accumulated via receive(), injectSweepAndCall, unrefunded overpaid ETH, or targets returning funds.
A third party calls execute, which delegates to Multicall3 aggregate3Value with arbitrary targets and ETH values from the router.
Public delegated Multicall3 aggregate3Value allows arbitrary targets and ETH values drawn from the router's own balance, so any nonzero router-held funds can be exfiltrated by a third party.
Direct theft of residual ETH and/or ERC20 stuck or dusted in the router occurs, independent of user mistakes.
Theft is likely in real-world routes that partially spend, refund, or rebate.
TrailsRouter's public execute/pullAmountAndExecute paths must not allow a caller to move the router's residual ETH or ERC20 funds to arbitrary targets outside the router's authorized route logic.
No access control or authorization restricts who may call execute/pullAmountAndExecute.

ambiguities: Report does not explicitly state that anyone (unauthenticated) can call execute/pullAmountAndExecute; public callability is asserted but not an explicit permissionless-caller statement.
No specific residual fund amount, token, or prior transaction establishing nonzero router balance is given; nonzero router-held funds are stated as a possibility.
Whether execute or pullAmountAndExecute is the primary exploited entry point is not disambiguated.
